A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CVCL/NeuronClassifier study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v3 reports original neuron-based classification experiments, concept-coverage measurements, AoA analysis, representation comparisons and classification examples.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results in Sections 4–5 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains CLIP-Dissect labeling, selection of the neuron most aligned with the target concept, and classification by maximum activation. Equations (1)–(7) and the inference procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same infant-trained models, Konkle classification task, ImageNet representation comparison, Broden concept analysis and AoA data. Ego4D and EPIC-KITCHENS are newly discussed as open-data examples, without evaluation on them.

E2.justification: The random-guess chance reference disappears from the out-of-vocabulary panel of v5 Figure 8, compared with v3 Figure 7, while remaining in the in-vocabulary panel. The CVCL-Random control and learned-model comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The datasets, five trials per class, main 4-way task, concept vocabulary and representation metrics remain unchanged. Appendix A.3 identifies the existing rightmost CVCL point as n = 31; inspection of both plots supports clarification of the retained experiment rather than a new evaluation setting.

E4.justification: The n-way sensitivity analysis, layer-wise comparisons and appendix success/failure examples are retained. The new Venn diagram and Appendix A.3 explain existing coverage restrictions without adding ablation or robustness evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same uncertainty reporting in Table 1 and the plots, along with the AoA test t(82) = 4.64, p < 0.0001. No new seed information, repeated-run counts or statistical procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Numerical tables and empirical findings are retained, but v5 Section 4.2 incorrectly reverses the CLIP comparison in prose by saying that vanilla underperforms. Both Table 1s still show 97.42% overall for vanilla versus 89.79% for NeuronClassifier. This is a limited change in reported findings, not measured performance.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation is retained. The CKA definition and Equation (8) move from v3 Section 5 to v5 Appendix B without a substantive mathematical revision or new proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim discovery of concepts beyond linguistic training inputs, training-free neuron-based recognition, improved in-vocabulary recognition and divergence in deeper representations. Revised contribution wording retains these claims and their scope.

C2.justification: v5 explicitly acknowledges inability to inspect the infant training data and absence of analysis on adult egocentric data. It also adds interpretations concerning similar outcomes across self-supervised methods and qualifies the semantic interpretability of individual neurons.

D1.justification: v5 adds a project-page address, documents institutional restrictions on dataset access and explains the existing n = 31 endpoint. Conversely, Section 4.1 omits v3's specified batch-normalization weights of one and bias initialization of zero; no actual initialization change is established.

R1.justification: Five cited works are added, covering superposition, infant development and brain imaging, and the Ego4D and EPIC-KITCHENS datasets. These provide limited additional context while retaining the established positioning relative to CVCL and network dissection.

P1.justification: The introduction and substantial portions of the results and layer-wise analysis are rewritten, with a more explicit hypothesis and revised explanatory narrative. Appendix A is reorganized, the CKA explanation moves to Appendix B, and limitations and an open-data discussion are added.

P2.justification: v5 adds the vocabulary-overlap Venn diagram, revises overview labels and several plot legends and captions, relocates existing displays, and sorts the appendix AoA tables. These are localized presentation changes; most visual evidence is retained.

improvement.justification: v5 makes the evaluation's class restrictions and existing n = 31 endpoint clearer and explicitly states data-access and applicability limitations, helping readers assess the retained evidence. These provide a modest net improvement despite the new erroneous CLIP comparison sentence and omitted initialization details; the central method and empirical support remain intact.
